summary.headline: Cummins India FY26 sales rose 18% to INR11,950 crore and Q4 PBT before exceptionals rose 20% to INR820 crore, with data centres at about 35% of Q4 domestic power gen revenue.
summary.overview: FY26 sales grew 18% YoY to INR11,950 crore, with domestic sales up 19% to INR9,961 crore and exports up 12% to INR1,989 crore. Q4 FY26 sales were INR2,963 crore, up 23% YoY but down 1% QoQ, and PBT before exceptional items rose 20% YoY to INR820 crore. Power generation domestic sales led growth, while industrial domestic sales were flat for the year. Management guided to moderate growth across segments in FY27, citing caution on geopolitics, commodity inflation and supply constraints despite robust domestic demand and order books.

segments.name: Power Generation domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR4,758 crore, up 24% YoY. Q4 sales INR1,294 crore, up 48% YoY and 21% QoQ; Q4 split was LHP INR55 crore, medium range INR177 crore, heavy duty INR108 crore, with the balance high horsepower.

segments.name: Distribution domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR3,278 crore, up 22% YoY. Q4 sales INR766 crore, up 21% YoY but down 18% QoQ. Management said price contributed little to growth.

segments.name: Industrial domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,650 crore, down 1% YoY. Q4 sales INR381 crore, up 1% YoY and down 18% QoQ; Q4 split was construction INR164 crore, rail INR111 crore, compressor INR59 crore, with the rest mining and defence.

segments.name: High horsepower exports
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR984 crore, up 20% YoY. Q4 sales INR217 crore, down 1% YoY and 7% QoQ.

segments.name: Low horsepower exports
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR807 crore, up 3% YoY. Q4 sales INR127 crore, down 18% YoY and 5% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: Management expects moderate growth across segments (power generation, industrial, distribution) in FY27, but did not quantify it.
Domestic demand is described as robust, with inquiries and order book strong, though management is cautious on geopolitics, commodity prices and inflation.
Exports: Europe and Asia Pacific growing modestly; Middle East and other markets weaker; no change in outlook.
Data centre engine mix expected to stay QSK60 for the next 2 years; QSK78 seen as more likely than QSK95 for larger sizes.
No major capex planned; continued spend on line modernisation and output expansion, following more than INR1,000 crore invested over the last 5 years.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation is about 70% across combined power gen and industrial facilities.
Capex has been ongoing for 10 years, focused on modernising lines and raising per-line output; no major capex plan announced.
Parent investing about $450 million to add 20 GW capacity by 2030, mainly for data centre engines; management expects this to shorten import lead times over time.
Lead times for imported large data centre engines have risen over the last few years due to global data centre demand; no figures given.
High horsepower order lead time is 3 to 6 months. Data centre orders typically come 6 to 12 months before site readiness, with revenue recognised on installation.
No local supply chain yet for BESS; management is working on it.
demand_pricing: Data centres were about 30-35% of FY26 domestic power gen revenue and about 35% in Q4; data centre inquiries have risen sharply since October 2025, from both hyperscalers and colocation players.
Hyperscaler revenue in Q4 was about INR250 crore, per management's answer to a Citi question.
Non-data centre power gen grew at higher double digits in FY26, with demand from manufacturing (solar cell, pharma), quick commerce dark stores, and luxury residential and commercial realty.
Power gen pricing is largely holding after the CPCB IV+ transition, though price competition continues in very low-cost lower ranges.
Industrial: railways and mining order books are building; compressor enters a down cycle; road construction is moderate.
Commodity inflation is being passed on with a lag; DEF is a very small part of distribution, so impact is limited.
Competition in HHP and data centres is intense but unchanged in intensity, per management; competitors are importing 95-litre engines.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 and Q4 power gen revenue came from data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres contributed 30-35% of FY26 domestic power gen revenue and about 35% in Q4. Distribution revenue for data centres sits on top of that and was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 hyperscaler revenue disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR250 crore of value in the quarter, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will larger engines (QSK78/QSK95) change the competitive landscape and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: QSK60 remains the near-term product for the next 2 years, and QSK78 looks more likely than QSK95. Management said no competitor makes 95-litre engines in India, and its value proposition covers service and solutions beyond cost, so margin impact is hard to call.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the commodity impact and how fast is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity increases are passed on with a lag. Order-book timing creates the challenge. DEF is a very small part of distribution. HHP lead times are 3 to 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity expansion planned, given 70% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capex is planned. Management is spending on line modernisation and output increases, and can tap global parent plants via an integrated supply chain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest and inquiries are high, but there is no sales pipeline yet and no local supply chain. Management is not sharing a contribution estimate or customer cohorts.

qa_highlights.question: Is price or volume driving growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is volume-led. Price and content gains apply mainly to CPCB IV+, and distribution growth comes from new solutions, not price.

risks_watch: Margin mix: data centre and CPCB IV+ growth relies on related-party QSK60 engines and imported QSK95 engines; management says margins are not affected, but it is an open question.
Commodity inflation and supply constraints (labour at suppliers, fuel costs, transport disruption from the war) may hit margins on existing orders, with pricing pass-through lagging.
Competitive pressure from imported large-engine players and local competitors in data centres, and price competition in low-end power gen.
Export demand is uncertain due to geopolitics; Middle East and other markets are weaker.
Distribution growth may slow as CPCB IV+ units leave warranty from June 2026, though management expects extended warranty packages to offset this.
Q4 FY26 sales were down 1% QoQ, and distribution and industrial fell sharply QoQ.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the trajectory of data centres and power gen, with the outlook for FY27 qualified as moderate. Management is cautious about commodities, geopolitics and supply constraints, and evasive on quantities (lead times, BESS contribution, currency effect on exports, extended warranty revenue booking, and distribution revenue for data centres).
key_quotes: So the inquiry velocity definitely increased quite a lot since October last year, and we continue to see that, Mohit.
For now, no major capital expenditure plan.
Pricing is largely sustaining across the range.

adds.what: Parent investing about $450 million to add 20 GW capacity by 2030, mainly for data centre engines (parent-level, not clearly company-owned line adds)

growth.why: Management guided only to unquantified moderate growth across segments in FY27, backed by robust domestic demand and order books but no specific capacity, timing or contracts; utilisation ~70% with no major capex planned, and the parent's $450M/20 GW expansion is a longer-dated, parent-level item.
